Emanuelsson, A. and Johnsson, F. (2022). The cost of CCS - a product chain analysis of the cement and pulp industries. Proceedings of the 16th International Conference on Greenhouse Gas Control Technologies (GHGT-16), Lyon, France, 23-27 October 2022. SSRN: https://ssrn.com/abstract=4280350

Locators are the printed GHGT-16 page numbers (1-15 = PDF pages; page 1 unnumbered). Product chain study (cement to high-speed railway; Kraft pulp to diaper) with plant-level cost tables. Loaded: cement plant (1.5 Mt/y) reference and with 90% amine CCS (per t cement: fixed and variable OPEX, emissions, captured CO2, annualised CCS capex converted to TCR with the printed 8%/25 y CRF, production cost label); amine capture unit per t CO2 (capture cost 99 EUR/t, 2.8 GJ/t steam, capex and incremental OPEX derived per t captured); Kraft pulp mill (0.8 Madt/y) reference and with CCS on recovery boiler and lime kiln (share-to-capture 77.5%, 2.11 t CO2/adt captured, capture cost 73 EUR/t). TRAPS: Table 3 CAPEX is ANNUALISED (EUR/t product/yr); capex here = annualised/CRF(8%, 25 y) with formula; cement energy 3025 MJ is per t CEMENT not clinker; the p.10 text misnames the pulp figures (says reference and CCS cost 328 and 270; Fig. 4 caption and Fig. 5b labels show 327.5/269.6 are the reference in base and high-cost scenarios, CCS 571.4/622.6). Cement and pulp plant data are reprinted from IEAGHG 2013 (cement) and Onarheim et al. 2016 (IEAGHG 2016/10, pulp). Price year EUR2020.
